name: 8th Mega Mock Test Series
instructions:
Please read the instructions carefully.

General Instructions:
1. The total duration of the examination is shown at the top. The clock counts down; when it reaches zero the test is submitted automatically. You do not have to submit when the time is over.
2. The question palette on the right shows the status of each question:
   Not Visited — you have not opened the question.
   Not Answered — you opened it but did not answer.
   Answered — you answered it.
   Marked for Review — you want to look at it again, no answer given.
   Answered & Marked for Review — answered, and will be counted unless you change it.
3. To answer: choose one option. Press "Save & Next" to save and go on, "Mark for Review & Next" to mark it and go on, or "Clear Response" to remove your answer.
4. To move to another question, click its number in the palette. Your selection on the current question is kept when you move.
5. Use the section names at the top to move between sections. You may return to any question until you submit.
6. Choose your language at the top right. The English text is always available.
7. Do not leave this screen, press the browser's back button or close the window. Switching away is recorded.

questions.passage: Nestled among towering Himalayan peaks, Sikkim was once an independent kingdom, ruled by its own royal family for centuries before becoming part of India in 1975. Unlike most other Indian states formed through the reorganisation of British-era provinces, Sikkim followed its own unique path to statehood, joining the Indian union through a special referendum in which its people voted overwhelmingly in favour of merging with India. Today, Gangtok, Sikkim's capital, sits high in the hills, surrounded by monasteries, terraced farms and views of Kanchenjunga, one of the world's tallest mountains. questions.passage: Nestled among towering Himalayan peaks, Sikkim was once an independent kingdom, ruled by its own royal family for centuries before becoming part of India in 1975. Unlike most other Indian states formed through the reorganisation of British-era provinces, Sikkim followed its own unique path to statehood, joining the Indian union through a special referendum in which its people voted overwhelmingly in favour of merging with India. Today, Gangtok, Sikkim's capital, sits high in the hills, surrounded by monasteries, terraced farms and views of Kanchenjunga, one of the world's tallest mountains. Despite being one of India's smallest states by population, Sikkim has gained recognition for becoming India's first fully organic farming state, banning chemical fertilisers and pesticides entirely. Visitors often remark that Sikkim's blend of monastery-dotted hillsides, environmental consciousness and unique political history make it one of India's most distinctive states, quietly different from nearly every other corner of the country.

questions.passage: Games and sports are as important as studies for children. When we play football, run races or swim, our body becomes strong and healthy. Sports also keep the mind fresh, so we can study better afterwards. On the playground, children learn many good habits. They learn to follow rules, to work as a team and to wait for their turn. questions.passage: Games and sports are as important as studies for children. When we play football, run races or swim, our body becomes strong and healthy. Sports also keep the mind fresh, so we can study better afterwards. On the playground, children learn many good habits. They learn to follow rules, to work as a team and to wait for their turn. A good player accepts defeat with a smile and does not boast after a victory. This is called sportsmanship. Sports also teach us discipline, because a player must practise at fixed times every day. A child who only studies and never plays becomes dull and tired. Therefore, every school should give its students enough time for games.

questions.passage: Kangla Fort stands on the banks of the Imphal River in the heart of Imphal. For many centuries, it was the seat of the kings of Manipur. The word 'Kangla' means 'dry land' in the old Meitei language. Inside the fort there are old temples, ponds and gates. Two large white dragon-like statues called Kangla Sha stand at the main gate. They are the symbol of the state. In 2004, the fort was handed back to the people of Manipur. Today it is a heritage site, and thousands of visitors come every year to learn about the history of Manipur.

questions.passage: Kangla Fort stands on the banks of the Imphal River in the heart of Imphal. For many centuries, it was the seat of the kings of Manipur. The word 'Kangla' means 'dry land' in the old Meitei language. Inside the fort there are old temples, ponds and gates. Two large white dragon-like statues called Kangla Sha stand at the main gate. They are the symbol of the state. In 2004, the fort was handed back to the people of Manipur. Today it is a heritage site, and thousands of visitors come every year to learn about the history of Manipur.
